verses.text: When Jesus and his disciples were near Jerusalem, close to Bethphage and Bethany at the Mount of Olives, he sent two of them ahead
and said, “Go into the village in front of you. As soon as you enter, you’ll find a young donkey tied up, one no one has ever ridden. Untie it and bring it here.
If anyone asks why you’re doing that, say, ‘The Lord needs it and will send it back here soon.’”
They went and found a young donkey tied outside by a doorway in the street. They untied it.
Some people standing there asked, “Why are you untying that young donkey?”
They answered as Jesus had told them, and the people let them go.
They brought the donkey to Jesus, laid their cloaks on it, and he sat on it.
Many people spread their cloaks on the road, while others spread leafy branches they’d cut in the fields.
Those walking ahead of Jesus and those following shouted, “Hosanna! Blessed is the one coming in the Lord’s name!
Blessed is the coming kingdom of our father David! Hosanna in the highest heaven!”
Jesus entered Jerusalem and went into the temple. After looking around at everything, he left for Bethany with the Twelve, since it was already late.
The next day, as they were leaving Bethany, Jesus was hungry.
He saw a fig tree in the distance with leaves on it, so he went to see if it had any fruit. But when he reached it, he found only leaves, because it wasn’t fig season.
He said to the tree, “May no one ever eat fruit from you again!” His disciples heard him.
They arrived in Jerusalem. Jesus went into the temple and began driving out the people buying and selling there. He overturned the tables of the money changers and the seats of those selling doves.
He wouldn’t let anyone carry goods through the temple courts.
Then he taught them: “Doesn’t Scripture say, ‘My house will be called a house of prayer for all nations’? But you’ve turned it into a hideout for robbers!”
The chief priests and legal experts heard about this and began looking for a way to kill him. They feared him, because the whole crowd was amazed at his teaching.
When evening came, Jesus and his disciples left the city.
The next morning, as they passed by, they saw the fig tree dried up from the roots.
Peter remembered and said, “Rabbi, look! The fig tree you cursed has dried up.”
Jesus answered, “Have faith in God.
I’m telling you the truth: if anyone says to this mountain, ‘Be lifted up and thrown into the sea,’ and doesn’t doubt in their heart but believes it will happen, it will be done.
So I tell you, whatever you ask for in prayer, believe that you’ve received it, and it will be yours.
Whenever you stand praying, forgive anyone you have something against, so your Father in heaven may forgive your sins too.
But if you don’t forgive, your Father in heaven won’t forgive your sins either.”
They returned to Jerusalem. As Jesus was walking in the temple courts, the chief priests, legal experts, and elders came to him.
They asked, “By what authority are you doing these things? Who gave you the authority to do them?”
Jesus said, “I’ll ask you one question. Answer me, and I’ll tell you by what authority I do these things.
John’s baptism—was it from heaven or from people? Answer me.”
They discussed it among themselves: “If we say, ‘From heaven,’ he’ll ask, ‘Then why didn’t you believe him?’
But if we say, ‘From people’”—they were afraid of the crowd, because everyone believed John was a prophet.
So they answered Jesus, “We don’t know.” Jesus said, “Then I won’t tell you by what authority I do these things.”
